title: Reconnect a car battery's positive cable
instruction: Reconnect the positive battery cable to the battery.
context: Reconnecting the battery is the last step of every battery replacement and terminal clean, routine daily work for automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023: 704,640 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2025) and a job many car owners do themselves. A clamp left riding high on the tapered post, or a pinch nut short of its torque, is a loose, high-resistance joint: it heats, cranks the engine slowly and eventually leaves the car unable to start; a nut forced past it deforms the lead clamp.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left; heights above the bench top. An inert dummy car battery, BCI group 24 size (26.0 x 17.3 x 22.5 cm, black polypropylene case, no acid and no charge, ballasted with dry sand to 18 kg, real lead posts), stands free on the bench, centre at x 30, y 0 (x 30.5, y -1.4 in seed 0, the screenshot's start), its long side along y and its two posts along its front edge, 2.2 cm in from the front face. The positive post (8.5 cm right of the battery's centre) is an SAE lead cone 19.5 mm across at its base and 17.5 mm at its top, 18 mm tall, on a 4 mm lead boss 28 mm across, red mark on top, red + on the lid behind it; the negative post (8.5 cm left of centre) is 17.9 mm at its base and 15.9 mm at its top, black mark, white - on the lid. The engine bay round it is fixed to the bench and set out from the battery: an inner fender to the robot's right, an 18 mm plywood board painted primer grey, 24.5 cm long and 30.5 cm tall (the hood line, 8 cm above the lid), standing on edge on two steel angle brackets clamped to the bench, its inner face 4.5 cm from the battery's right-hand end, running from 2 cm in front of the battery's front face to 5.2 cm behind its back face; and a hold-down bar, a black steel flat bar 25 x 6 mm and 30 cm long on a 2 mm rubber strip, lying across the lid along its length, its centre line 1.65 cm in from the back face, on two 8 mm steel J-bolts that stand 1.2 cm beyond each battery end in steel foot plates clamped to the bench (nuts finger-tight, the bar just touching the lid). The bay's front, toward the robot, is open. The positive cable, red 4 AWG battery cable 8.6 mm across, is anchored in a black rubber-lined steel P-clip on a cable stand 1.5 cm behind the battery's back face, in line with the positive post (a 25 x 6 mm steel flat-bar upright on a 10 x 6 cm steel base plate clamped to the bench; the clip's axis 24.3 cm above the bench, 1.8 cm above the lid). From the clip the cable runs straight forward over the hold-down bar and the lid, 16.6 cm, to its clamp; behind the clip it runs down to the bench. The clamp sits on the positive post, held 6 mm above its seat by the cable: a lead top-post clamp, 0.14 kg with its lug, a 12-sided collar 31.1 mm across its flats and 16 mm tall, its bore tapered like the post; two ears either side of a 4 mm split, reaching 18 mm out from the collar's front face, with an M8 x 1.25 pinch bolt across them 13 mm out from the collar (carriage head on the right ear, a 13 mm steel hex nut, 6.5 mm thick, on the left, a white line across its face), and a crimp lug at the back. The nut is run down by hand only, until it stops against the ear, the split still open. A 13 mm combination wrench (chrome vanadium steel, 18.1 cm long, 0.105 kg, 12-point box end and open end), instrumented to record its torque at the nut: two strain-gauge bridges on the shank's narrow edges, 3 cm and 7 cm from the box end's centre (the gripper holds the handle further out), under a thin protective coat, on a slack 2 mm lead (6 g/m) that leaves the shank 8 cm from the box end and hangs from a hook 60 cm above the tool stand, to a two-channel strain-gauge amplifier and logger sampling at 100 Hz. The torque at the nut is the two bending readings extended in a straight line to the box end's centre, so it does not depend on where the handle is held. It stands open end down in a tool stand centred at x 10.5, y 10 (x 11.45, y 9.4 in seed 0): a steel pedestal 6 x 7 x 12 cm with an orange-painted wooden holder on top, 5 x 4.4 x 3 cm, with a 9 mm slot along x; 2.5 kg in all. Each trial's seed moves the battery, the bay and the cable stand together by up to 1.2 cm in x and 1.5 cm in y, tips the clamp by up to 2.5 degrees and turns it by up to 4 degrees as it is set down, and moves the tool stand by up to 1.5 cm in x and 1 cm in y. Both grippers start open at the ready pose, the right one outside the fender.
scoring: Measured at the end. Seated: a 1.0 mm feeler gauge does not go under the collar's outer edge at its front, back, left or right; the clamp square to the post within 2 degrees and centred on it within 3 mm. Tight: the nut holds 5 to 7 N m, the usual torque for a top-post clamp's pinch nut: a dial torque wrench with a 13 mm socket, turned clockwise on the nut, reads 5 to 7 N m as the nut starts to move (the sim reads the nut's modelled torque). Never over-tightened: the nut was never taken past 7 N m during the trial, measured, not inferred from the nut's angle: the instrumented wrench's logged torque at the nut, tightening direction, never stayed above 7 N m for 0.15 s (15 samples in a row at 100 Hz), and the dial wrench's end reading is at most 7 N m. Tightened off the log counts as not verified, scored as over-tightened: the nut turned clockwise more than 5 degrees with the box end off it (the open end or a finger on it; from the trial video, by the white line on the nut's face). The final torque goes on with the box end, which holds all 12 points where an open end can round the nut, and it is the end the gauges measure. A trial with no log is void and is run again. The sim's wrench records the torque passing through its box end into the nut, 20 times a second, and is scored by the same rules. Lug in line: within 10 degrees of the cable's run, straight back to its clip. 1.0: seated, tight, never over-tightened, lug in line, the wrench's box end at least 2 cm from the nut and the wrench not on or against the battery (no part of it more than 3 cm above the bench within 1 cm of the battery's outline; a steel wrench left on a battery can bridge its posts), every gripper finger pad at least 4 cm from every part of the clamp (collar, ears, nut, lug, and the cable up to its clip) and of the wrench (fingertip positions from the arms' logged joint angles, or a photo with a scale), and the clamp, nut and wrench each moving less than 1 cm and 0.1 rad over the last second (the video's last second), held for 1 s. 0.75: seated, tight, never over-tightened and lug in line, but the wrench on the nut or on or against the battery, a finger pad within 4 cm, or something moving. 0.5: the same, lug 10 to 30 degrees out. 0.25: seated, tight and never over-tightened with the lug over 30 degrees out; or seated with the nut under 5 N m at the end (loose), or over 7 N m at the end or in the wrench's log at any time before (over-tightened, even if backed off after), or tightened with the box end off (not verified). 0: the clamp high or crooked (the bore closes on the post wherever the collar is: tightened high, it is pinched high; let go before that, the cable springs it back up), off the positive post or on the negative post, the battery moved more than 5 mm, or nothing done.
reset_notes: Use the inert dummy battery (no acid, no charge). With a live battery instead, fit a rubber boot over the negative post before every trial, so a steel wrench across the posts cannot short them. Loosen the nut a full turn, lift the clamp off the post, set it back on and let go: the cable holds it where it rests, collar 6 mm above the boss (check with a 6 mm drill shank). Run the nut down clockwise by hand until it stops against the ear (finger-tight, no tool): that is the start. Put the wrench back in its holder; set the battery, the bay (fender board and hold-down J-bolts), the cable stand and the tool stand on the trial's marks, and run the hold-down nuts down finger-tight until the bar just touches the lid. Load check: pushing the cable down 3 mm from where it rests, 6 cm behind the post, takes 12 N (a push gauge); if less, move the cable stand closer to the battery; if more, farther. A clamp taken past 7 N m may be deformed: replace it. Wrench check, before each session and after any drop: box end on a 13 mm hex bolt held in a vice, handle level, logger zeroed with nothing hung; a 4.08 kg weight hung 15.0 cm from the box end's centre must log 6.0 N m, and a 6.12 kg weight hung 10.0 cm out must log 6.0 N m, each within 0.2 N m; the dial torque wrench on the same bolt cross-checks it. Before each trial, zero the logger with the wrench standing in its holder, start the log, and keep the trace (one file per trial) with the video.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, real sizes and masses (nut 30 g, real 7 g). Cable: a 4,000 N/m spring. Nut: friction of 1 N m, then 1 N m more per 30 degrees once the bore closes (modelled; real trials are scored from the wrench's log instead). On the nut the box end is a joint that passes the full torque to the hand (6 N m is 44 N on the handle). The wrench's gauges and lead are not modelled: its reading is the torque wound into the nut's friction while it is on. Nut inertia padded, speed capped. More: README.
